title: The “Genre-Bending” Screenplay Engine
use_cases: Implement when transforming long-form narrative content while maintaining structural integrity
Configure when architectural consistency is required across large-scale document processing
Use when performing deep stylistic genre transformations on existing creative works
Implement when preventing LLM hallucinations in complex, multi-page text handling
content:
The mission sounded simple enough: Build a feature that takes an existing screenplay and fundamentally transforms its genre. We wanted users to be able to take a serious Drama and rewrite it as a slapstick Comedy, or turn a Western into a Film Noir.

But here’s the kicker: You can’t just tell an LLM to “make it funny.”

If you treat a 120-page script as one big string of text, the AI will inevitably hallucinate. It might change the genre, but it will lose the plot. We needed a system that ensured narrative consistency and structural integrity while performing a deep stylistic transformation. We needed the AI to understand that even if the setting changes from an office to a spaceship, the emotional subtext of the scene must remain intact.

The Tech Stack

We architected this as a client-side orchestrator calling a stateless server-side API.

- The Muscle: A stateless API endpoint that performs distinct actions like “analyze”, “bible”, “mutate”, and “write”.
- The Orchestrator: A client-side service that manages the long-running process. It handles splitting the screenplay into atomic units (scenes), tracking progress, and stitching the final result back together.
- The Brains: Google Gemini LLM (via the backend API).

The breakthrough came when we stopped trying to rewrite the script linearly. Instead, we adopted a Map-Reduce-Mutate-Execute architecture. We realized that to rewrite a story successfully, the AI first had to understand it completely, separating the analysis phase from the writing phase.

Data flow diagram

So, how do we actually pull this off? We don’t just ask the AI to “rewrite the script.” That’s a rookie move. Instead, we treat the LLM as a sophisticated data processing engine. We break the job down into a 5-Phase Pipeline that separates understanding the story from generating the new version.

Here is how the sausage is made:

First, we need to ground the AI. We ingest the entire raw screenplay text just to get a high-level summary.

- Why: You can’t rewrite Scene 1 effectively if you don’t know the movie ends in a tragedy. This summary is injected into every subsequent phase to ensure the AI knows where it is going.
- The Goal: Establish a “Big Picture” understanding of the narrative arc.
